articles.title_original: Tuning Structural, Mechanical, Electrical, and Thermal Behavior of Polypropylene via Graphene Nanoplatelet Integration
articles.title_en: Graphene Nanoplatelets Tune Polypropylene Properties
articles.summary_en: A study examines how integrating graphene nanoplatelets changes polypropylene’s structural, mechanical, electrical, and thermal behavior. The research may inform graphene-enhanced polymer composites with tailored multifunctional performance.

articles.title_original: Occurrence of the anomalous quantum Hall effect in monolayer graphene
articles.title_en: Monolayer graphene’s anomalous quantum Hall effect explained through Dirac physics
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract This paper provides a pedagogical overview of the anomalous quantum Hall effect in monolayer graphene subjected to a magnetic field perpendicular to the graphene plane. The energy states of the fundamental charge carriers – electrons and holes – are examined usingthe Dirac–Weyl framework, showing that their Landau level spectrum depends on the square root of the quantum number n, unlike the uniform spacing found in two-dimensional nonrelativistic charge carriers. A distinctive feature of graphene is the zero-energy Landau level, which lies exactly at the Dirac point and is therefore shared equally between the conduction and valence bands. Its spin–valley degeneracy is the same as that of every other level, but only half of its states are counted on the electron side of charge neutrality. This is what produces the characteristic half-integer quantization of the Hall conductivity, the hallmark of the anomalous quantum Hall effect in graphene. The topological origin of this phenomenon is discussed: the pseudospin structure of massless Dirac fermions imparts a Berry phase of π to the Bloch states when encircling a Dirac point, shifting the Landau level index by ½ compared to the conventional Schrödinger case. The connection between the degeneracy counting argument and the topological description via the Thouless–Kohmoto–Nightingale–den Nijs (TKNN) formula and the Chern number is made explicit, demonstrating that these two approaches are complementary aspects of the same underlying physics.
articles.summary_en: The paper reviews how graphene’s zero-energy Landau level and π Berry phase produce half-integer quantization of Hall conductivity. It connects the physical explanation to Chern numbers and the TKNN formalism, providing a pedagogical account of the effect.

articles.title_original: Monolithic graphene−qBIC resonators for electrically tunable terahertz modulation
articles.title_en: Monolithic graphene qBIC resonator enables tunable THz modulation
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Terahertz (THz) modulators are essential components for dynamic wavefront control in imaging, sensing, and wireless communication systems. However, practical THz modulators require simultaneous optimization of multiple functional metrics, including modulation depth, resonance quality, insertion loss, switching speed, and device integration, which are often difficult to balance within a single device architecture. Graphene is an attractive active material because of its electrical tunability, high carrier mobility, and compatibility with planar integration, but its intrinsically weak interaction with THz waves limits the modulation efficiency of pristine monolayer devices. Here, we demonstrate a monolithic graphene-quasi-bound-state-in-the-continuum (qBIC) resonator platform that addresses this multidimensional performance trade-off. By integrating patterned graphene within symmetry-broken double-rod metallic resonators, the dissipative loss of a high-Q qBIC resonance can be continuously controlled through electrostatic gating. The fabricated modulator achieves a modulation depth of 35%, a resonance bandwidth of 0.12 THz centered at 1.1 THz, an equivalent Q factor of 9.28, a 3 dB modulation speed of 14 kHz, and a low insertion loss of 2.08 dB. These results demonstrate balanced optimization of key modulation metrics in a compact, planar architecture, providing a practical route toward active THz photonic devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrate a graphene-integrated quasi-bound-state-in-the-continuum resonator that achieves electrically tunable terahertz modulation with 35% depth, 14 kHz speed, and 2.08 dB insertion loss. The planar architecture addresses trade-offs among modulation efficiency, bandwidth, switching speed, and integration for THz photonic devices.

articles.title_original: The First Magic Angle Beyond the Chiral Limit in Twisted Bilayer Graphene
articles.title_en: Study Explains Stability of the First Magic Angle in Twisted Bilayer Graphene
articles.excerpt_original: We develop a squared-Hamiltonian description of twisted bilayer graphene beyond the chiral limit to explain why the first magic angle remains robust under lattice relaxation, while higher-order magic angles are strongly destabilized. Starting from the non-chiral Bistritzer--MacDonald model with finite same-sublattice tunneling, we show that lattice relaxation reshapes the effective confinement landscape rather than acting as a simple perturbation of the chiral theory. A central result is that the realistic relaxation-renormalized tunneling ratio lies close to a special confinement point where the oscillatory part of the symmetric confinement potential nearly cancels. This places realistic twisted bilayer graphene near a nearly uniform confinement regime. At the same time, finite same-sublattice tunneling activates an additional inter-sublattice current-like channel that competes with the chiral orbital channel. The first magic angle survives because these confinement and current-like contributions remain balanced, whereas higher-order magic angles lose this balance through stronger remote-band hybridization and enhanced real-space localization around AA regions. Our results provide a single-particle mechanism for the breakdown of the chiral magic-angle hierarchy and clarify why the experimentally relevant first magic angle remains the most stable remnant of the chiral flat-band structure.
articles.summary_en: Researchers develop a non-chiral theoretical model showing that lattice relaxation and competing current-like effects preserve the first magic angle while destabilizing higher-order magic angles. The findings clarify the robustness of experimentally relevant flat-band behavior in twisted bilayer graphene.

articles.title_original: Multilayer MXene (Ti3C2Tx) Sheets with Redistribution of Aluminium (Al) Nanoparticles as Al@MXene Anode for Superior Lithium-Ion Battery Performance
articles.title_en: Al-Modified MXene Anodes Show Improved Lithium-Ion Battery Performance
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract High-capacity, stable-performance batteries are needed to meet current energy storage demand. However, high-capacity batteries require optimization of the anode, cathode, and electrolyte. Herein, we synthesized novel MXene (Ti3C2Tx) sheets with redistribution of ‘Al’ nanoparticles formed by Ostwald ripening during hydrofluoric acid (HF) etching of MAX (Ti3AlC2) for anode performance evaluation in a lithium-ion battery (LIB). The imaging and spectroscopy studies clearly evidenced the ‘Al’ nanoparticle modification on MXene sheets and an increment of inter-layer distance from 0.8 nm to more than 3 nm through HF treatment of MAX to MXene. The electrochemical performance of optimized Al@Ti3C2Tx shows a superior LIB anode performance with a specific capacity of 546 mAh/g at 0.1 A/g current density with charge transfer resistance 110 Ohm, whereas the MAX sample shows a 56 mAh/g at 1 A/g with 190 Ohms. Characterization and electrochemical results indicate that the redistributed ‘Al’ nanoparticles on the Ti3C2Tx surface act as an ‘inter-metallic interface’ which affects local charge density and results in the superior anode performance of Al@Ti3C2Tx in the LIB coin cell. This work demonstrates that the ‘Al’ nanoparticles redistributed multilayer Ti3C2Tx sheets with superior LIB anode performance, making it a promising candidate for high-energy density LIB energy storage devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed multilayer Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene sheets bearing redistributed aluminium nanoparticles for lithium-ion battery anodes. The optimized Al@MXene delivered 546 mAh/g at 0.1 A/g, substantially outperforming the reported MAX reference, indicating potential for higher-energy-density storage.

articles.title_original: Exploring the effect of few-layer graphene on 3D neuronal differentiation scaffolds
articles.title_en: Few-layer graphene enhances neuronal differentiation in 3D hydrogel scaffolds
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT The rising incidence of neurodegenerative diseases has driven the development of advanced 3D scaffolds that better mimic the native neural environment. By incorporating tunable biomaterials such as hydrogels, these systems enable the investigation of how physical cues, including stiffness, spatial confinement, and matrix architecture, regulate neuronal cell behaviour and differentiation. In this study, few-layer graphene (FLG) was incorporated into a photopolymerizable chitosan–acrylamide hydrogel to develop a biomimetic 3D scaffold for neural tissue engineering. The incorporation of FLG enhanced SH-SY5Y cell viability and promoted differentiation towards a neuron-like phenotype under basal conditions. Moreover, FLG-containing hydrogels showed an enhanced differentiation response when combined with established biochemical differentiation factors. In particular, the CHI-AM_0.2FLG formulation exhibited an approximately two-fold higher normalized MAP2 fluorescence intensity following BDNF treatment than the corresponding FLG-free condition. These findings suggest that the physicochemical environment provided by low FLG incorporation may enhance the cellular response to biochemical differentiation cues. Overall, FLG acts as an active component of the hydrogel matrix, modulating cellular behavior rather than functioning solely as a structural filler. Such 3D in vitro platforms may contribute to the development of complementary approaches that reduce reliance on animal models animal models by providing physiologically relevant systems for investigating neurite-like outgrowth and mechanisms relevant to neurodegenerative diseases.
articles.summary_en: Researchers incorporated few-layer graphene into a chitosan–acrylamide hydrogel to create a 3D neural tissue-engineering scaffold. The graphene-containing formulation improved SH-SY5Y cell viability and approximately doubled MAP2 fluorescence after BDNF treatment, indicating enhanced neuron-like differentiation.

articles.title_original: Ammonia-Assisted Nb2CTx MXenes with Tuneable Layering and Surface Chemistry for Superior Li and Na-Ion Energy Storage
articles.title_en: Ammonia-Assisted Nb₂CTₓ MXene Enables HF-Free Li- and Na-Ion Anodes
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract MXenes are widely recognized for battery applications due to their rapid ion-intercalation capability and excellent cycling stability. However, conventional synthesis methods often involve hazardous HF, prolonged reaction times, and complex procedures, limiting their practical implementation. Here, we present an efficient and sustainable ammonia-assisted hydrothermal strategy for synthesizing Nb2CTx MXene from the Nb2AlC MAX phase using a mild etchant, providing a safe, cost-effective, and scalable route. The as-prepared MXene was further delaminated via probe sonication, yielding an expanded interlayer spacing of ~9.7 Å and optimized surface functionalities. XPS reveals an oxygen-rich (-O/-OH) surface that promotes Li⁺/Na⁺ interaction and ion diffusion, consistent with the enhanced reversibility observed in CV and GCD profiles. As an anode, Nb2CTx delivers a high reversible discharge capacity of 484 mAh g⁻¹ at 0.1 A g⁻¹ with stable cycling over 100 cycles in lithium-ion batteries, and 198 mAh g⁻¹ at 0.1 A g⁻¹ over 100 cycles in sodium-ion batteries. Ex-situ post-mortem XRD confirms that Nb2CTx retains structural integrity and electrochemical stability after 100 cycles. Importantly, hydrothermal etching eliminates concentrated HF while producing well-exfoliated flakes. Combined structural, surface, and electrochemical analyses reveal the origins of its performance, providing a blueprint for next-generation sustainable MXene electrodes.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a milder ammonia-assisted hydrothermal method to produce delaminated Nb₂CTₓ MXene without concentrated HF. The material delivered reversible capacities of 484 mAh g⁻¹ in lithium-ion cells and 198 mAh g⁻¹ in sodium-ion cells at 0.1 A g⁻¹, with stable cycling over 100 cycles.

articles.title_original: Fast Programming of in‐Plane Hyperbolic Phonon Polariton Optics through Van der Waals Crystals Using the Phase‐Change Material In 3 SbTe 2
articles.title_en: Optically Reconfigurable Hyperbolic Polariton Optics Programmed in Phase-Change Material
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT The high directionality of hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs) has opened radically new ways to route and steer the flow of energy at the nanoscale. However, launching HPhPs requires fabricating efficient and precisely aligned polariton launching structures, what remains time‐consuming and expensive with conventional nanofabrication approaches. Recently, using visible laser pulses, polariton launching structures have been programmed into the plasmonic phase‐change material In 3 SbTe 2 . Here, we leverage this approach to tailor in‐plane hyperbolic polaritons by programming launching and confining nanostructures through α‐MoO 3 flakes deposited onto In 3 SbTe 2 . Importantly, optical programming after flake deposition enables alignment of launching stripes to the flake's [001]‐axis, essential to control the directional polariton propagation. We showcase i) an optically programmed focusing disk, showing similar tuning ranges and confinement as focusing by gold disks; and ii) a first experimental realization toward a nanocavity for in‐plane HPhPs created by reconfiguring the single disk to a double disk structure, tailoring the confinement by simply reprogramming the disk distance. Our fabrication scheme offers fast turnaround times, flexible alignment, and the opportunity to reversibly reconfigure structures within 30 s. Thus, it is a fast, efficient, and versatile way to tailor propagation and confinement of highly directional polaritons on demand.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated laser-programmable launching, focusing, and nanocavity structures for hyperbolic phonon polaritons in α-MoO₃ flakes on In₃SbTe₂. The structures can be aligned after deposition and reversibly reconfigured in about 30 seconds, enabling flexible nanoscale energy routing.

articles.title_original: Proof of concept of a graphene-based reconfigurable frequency multiplier fabricated within the 2D Experimental Pilot Line
articles.title_en: Graphene circuit demonstrates reconfigurable frequency multiplication
articles.excerpt_original: Graphene intrinsic carrier ambipolarity enables unique circuit functionalities that would otherwise require significantly more complex circuit topologies to achieve with conventional semiconductors. Yet, translating these properties into practical, wafer-scale electronic systems remains a significant challenge. Here, we present an experimental proof of concept of a reconfigurable frequency multiplier based on a single split-gate graphene field-effect transistor. The devices used for this demonstration were externally fabricated through a multi-project wafer tape-out of the 2D Experimental Pilot Line, an initiative aimed at providing a scalable platform service for the manufacturing of 2D-material-based devices and circuits. The split-gate architecture synthesizes a W-shaped transfer characteristic within a single device enabling electrically reconfigurable frequency multiplication by factors of × 2, × 3, and × 4 without requiring multiple transistors or fixed fabrication-dependent tuning mechanisms. Time-domain measurements and spectral analysis confirm harmonic reconfiguration, yielding spectral purities of 48% for the doubler, 69% for the tripler, and 19% for the quadrupler at an input frequency of 100 kHz. This constitutes the first demonstration of a reconfigurable circuit using devices from the multi-project wafer 2D-EPL platform, representing a step forward in the integration complexity achievable with wafer-scale graphene technology.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated a single split-gate graphene transistor that electrically reconfigures frequency multiplication by factors of 2, 3, and 4. Fabrication through the 2D Experimental Pilot Line provides a proof of concept for integrating graphene circuits on a wafer-scale platform, though reported spectral purity varies substantially by multiplication factor.

articles.title_original: Contrasting roles of the superexchange and direct exchange interactions in the metal-insulator transitions of the 2D ferromagnetic $1T$-Fe$X_2$ ($X$=Cl, Br, I) monolayers
articles.title_en: Exchange interactions govern metal–insulator transitions in 2D iron halides
articles.excerpt_original: Within the rapidly growing family of two-dimensional (2D) materials, 2D ferromagnetic (FM) materials have attracted a great deal of recent attention. The ferromagnetism in 2D FM materials originates from the underlying exchange interactions. In particular, metal-insulator transitions (MITs) in 2D FM materials induced via various modulation strategies is critical to the design of 2D electronic devices with reduced sizes (e.g. transistor). However, the critical behaviors of exchange interactions and their effects on the Curie temperatures near MITs remains to be clarified. By taking the 2D FM 1T-FeX2 (X=Cl, Br, I) monolayers as the testbeds, we computationally study the critical behaviors of the exchange interactions in the vicinity of the MITs driven by the on-site Coulomb electron-electon interactions. The FM superexchange interactions and the direct exchange interactions are found to energetically favor the halfmetallic and semiconducting states, respectively. In addition, the halfmetallic states have the stronger FM couplings and thus the higher Curie temperatures. This study provides a comprehensive understanding of the interrelations between MITs and exchange interactions and could be useful for the device design requiring both MITs and exchange-interaction related magnetic properties, particularly robust magnetic ordering and higher Curie temperatures, in 2D FM materials.
articles.summary_en: Computational research on ferromagnetic 1T-FeX₂ (X=Cl, Br, I) monolayers finds that superexchange favors half-metallic states, while direct exchange favors semiconducting states. The results link electronic phase control with Curie temperature and could inform transistor and other 2D magnetic-device designs.

articles.title_original: Graphene-tuned near-zero index waveguides [Invited]
articles.title_en: Graphene-tuned waveguides enable broadband near-zero-index response
articles.excerpt_original: We demonstrate that a graphene-based guided-wave structure can realize an effective epsilon-and-mu-near-zero (EMNZ) medium over an exceptionally broad bandwidth. The proposed platform consists of a parallel-plate waveguide in which a graphene sheet is placed in deep subwavelength proximity to a PEC wall, forming a tunable reactive boundary that governs phase accumulation and modal dispersion. By exploiting this configuration, both the effective permittivity and permeability of the guided mode are simultaneously driven toward zero across a wide frequency range, yielding a robust EMNZ response that is not tied to narrow resonant phenomena. Closed-form dispersion relations reveal how the graphene conductivity and subwavelength spacing jointly control the effective material parameters. Full-wave simulations validate the analytical predictions and confirm the existence of a broadband regime characterized by extremely long guided wavelengths and negligible phase advance over electrically short sections. These results establish graphene-loaded waveguides as a simple, scalable, and physically transparent route to broadband EMNZ metamaterials, with direct relevance to integrated photonic and electromagnetic devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrate a graphene-loaded parallel-plate waveguide that achieves broadband epsilon-and-mu-near-zero behavior through tunable graphene conductivity and deep-subwavelength placement near a conducting wall. Simulations support the potential of the platform for integrated photonic and electromagnetic devices.

articles.title_original: Non-Markovian dynamics of a qubit on the zigzag edge of photonic graphene

articles.excerpt_original: We present an analytical study of the dynamics of a qubit coupled to the zigzag edge of a photonic honeycomb lattice. Leveraging a resolvent operator approach and exact lattice Green's functions, we map the spectrum of qubit-photon bound states and complex poles to uncover the long-time scaling laws of the qubit population. Unlike a qubit coupled to the bulk of graphene, the presence of a zero-energy flat band connecting the Dirac points suppresses long-time branch-cut-induced tails, instead driving damped Rabi oscillations. Potential experimental platforms are briefly discussed.
articles.summary_en: Researchers analytically examine a qubit coupled to the zigzag edge of a photonic honeycomb lattice. They find that a zero-energy flat band suppresses long-time decay tails and produces damped Rabi oscillations, contrasting with bulk graphene coupling.

articles.title_original: Resonance-engineered Ti3C2Tx MXene metasurface for ultra-broadband absorption-dominated green electromagnetic interference shielding
articles.title_en: Ti3C2Tx MXene metasurface enables broadband absorption-dominant EMI shielding
articles.excerpt_original: The rapid advancement of information technologies necessitates the development of adaptive and green electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials capable of real-time response, high efficiency, and minimal secondary reflection. Here, we report a scaled Ti3C2Tx MXene-based Multi-arm Jointed-cross (S-MXJC) metasurface that achieves ultrabroadband, absorption-dominated green EMI shielding, with a shielding effectiveness (SE) exceeding 83.78 dB and an average green index (gs) of 64.55 across the 8.2-12.4 GHz (X-band) frequency range. The strategic scaling of meta-atoms enables the distribution of resonances over a broad frequency range, while precise capacitive-inductive coupling ensures impedance matching with free space, thereby suppressing the secondary reflections. Utilizing the high electrical conductivity (σ ~ 105 S/m) and intrinsic multi-scale polarization losses of Ti3C2Tx MXene, the gradient metasurface maintains a high gs value across the entire frequency range, confirming the continuous absorption-dominated behaviour. Furthermore, electromagnetic equivalent circuit modelling (ECM), validated by full-wave CST simulations, elucidates the underlying mechanism by which the distributed sheet resistance of Ti3C2Tx MXene synergizes with S-MXJC resonance to reconcile high conductivity with absorption dominance. This work establishes a flexible and lightweight metasurface platform that delivers high-efficiency, broadband green EMI shielding, offering a promising pathway for next-generation flexible electronic systems. articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a flexible Ti3C2Tx MXene metasurface that achieved more than 83.78 dB shielding effectiveness across the X-band, with reduced secondary reflection through absorption-dominated operation. articles.title_original: Magnetized Graphene-Based Metasurface for Terahertz Cross-Polarization Conversion
articles.title_en: Magnetized graphene metasurface enables broadband terahertz polarization conversion
articles.excerpt_original: A broadband magnetically tunable reflective metasurface based on magnetized graphene is presented for terahertz cross-polarization conversion. The metasurface adopts a three-layer stacked configuration consisting of a patterned graphene resonator, a dielectric spacer, and a metallic ground plane. Under perpendicular magnetic induction, magnetized graphene exhibits in-plane gyrotropic surface conductivity featuring prominent Hall components. Coupled with resonant interactions within the asymmetric unit cell, this intrinsic property facilitates the efficient conversion of normally incident y-polarized terahertz waves into x-polarized counterparts. Numerical results demonstrate that under an external magnetic induction of 3 T, the polarization conversion ratio exceeds 0.95 across the 1.40–2.80 THz band, generating a relative bandwidth of 66.7%. Moreover, its polarization conversion response can be dynamically modulated by varying the external magnetic induction. These simulated results verify that the designed metasurface is a promising candidate for gate-free, broadband, and reconfigurable terahertz polarization manipulation systems.
articles.summary_en: Researchers simulated a three-layer magnetized graphene metasurface that converts normally incident terahertz waves between orthogonal polarizations. articles.title_original: Ladder‐Type Polymer Enables Dual‐Directional Phonon Bridging in Thermally Conductive h‐BN/TOCNF Film
articles.title_en: Ladder Polymer Improves Thermal Conductivity in h-BN/Cellulose Films
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT The persistent trade‐off between preserving the intrinsic thermal conductivity of fillers and minimizing interfacial thermal resistance remains a critical bottleneck in polymer‐based thermal interface materials (TIMs). Herein, we address this challenge through a “dual‐directional bridging” strategy using poly(benzimidazobenzophenanthroline) (BBL), a rigid ladder‐type conjugated polymer, as an interfacial mediator. Unlike conventional modifiers, BBL features an extended superplane architecture that concurrently establishes maximized π – π interlocking with the hexagonal boron nitride (h‐BN) basal plane and weaves dense hydrogen‐bonding networks with the TEMPO‐oxidized cellulose nanofiber (TOCNF) matrix. Combined spectroscopic analyses and solvent‐corrected DFT calculations support π ‐associated coupling between BBL and h‐BN together with hydrogen‐bonding interactions between BBL and TOCNF, increasing the calculated interfacial binding energy from 0.85 to 2.86 eV under an aqueous environment. Crucially, this creates a continuous “dual‐directional phonon bridge” that substantially mitigates interfacial thermal resistance and localized phonon scattering, all without disrupting the intrinsic h‐BN lattice. Consequently, the BBL@h‐BN/TOCNF film achieves in‐plane and through‐plane thermal conductivities of 8.78 and 1.18 W m −1 K −1 , outperforming standard commercial thermal silicone grease and demonstrating superior heat extraction in simulated high‐power CPU cooling. Overall, this work establishes a rational structural paradigm to unlock the macroscopic thermo‐mechanical potential of two‐dimensional (2D) composites for next‐generation electronics.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used a rigid ladder-type polymer to bridge hexagonal boron nitride and cellulose nanofibers, reducing interfacial thermal resistance without disrupting the filler lattice. The resulting film reached 8.78 W/m·K in-plane and 1.18 W/m·K through-plane conductivity, outperforming commercial thermal silicone grease in simulated CPU cooling.

articles.title_original: Optoelectronic oscillation in a two-dimensional floating-gate transistor for neuromorphic computing
articles.title_en: Graphene Floating-Gate Transistor Enables Programmable Neuromorphic Waveforms
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Oscillator-inspired neural computing offers a promising route toward energy-efficient information processing, yet its practical implementation is constrained by the lack of compact hardware platforms capable of generating programmable temporal signals. Here, we present a two-dimensional MoS2/hBN/few-layer graphene floating-gate transistor as a programmable optoelectronic waveform generator. The temporal waveforms emerge from the dynamic competition between gate-induced charge injection and ultraviolet-assisted charge erasure in the floating gate, which drives periodic modulation of the channel conductance. The output frequency can be adjusted from 1 Hz to 10 kHz, while the waveform profile is regulated through gate-voltage programming, illumination intensity, and drain bias. Two coupled devices further demonstrate externally programmable in-phase and anti-phase temporal signal generation, and the experimentally measured dynamics are incorporated into numerical simulations of associative memory recall and graph-coloring tasks. By enabling programmable temporal signal generation in floating-gate transistors, this work establishes a compact hardware building block for oscillator-inspired neuromorphic computing and multifunctional temporal information processing.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a MoS₂/hBN/few-layer graphene floating-gate transistor that generates programmable waveforms from 1 Hz to 10 kHz through optically assisted charge dynamics. Coupled devices demonstrated phase control, with simulations indicating potential for associative-memory and graph-coloring tasks in neuromorphic computing.

articles.title_original: 2D van der Waals materials as saturable absorbers to characterize non-linear optical properties in nanomaterials
articles.title_en: Review examines 2D van der Waals materials as saturable absorbers for nonlinear-optics characterization
articles.excerpt_original: The main aim of this review is to identify the limitations for characterizing the high magnitude non-linear optical (NLO) response in nanomaterials due to quantum confinement in 3-Dimensions (3D), 2D, or 1D. We present basics on NLO response of second (χ 2 ) and third order (χ 3 ), briefly describing the experimental parameters determining their magnitude and their significance. We study the enhanced NLO response with a few examples in such reduced-dimensional semiconductors and further compare the hackneyed techniques and their heterodox modifications employed to study such higher-order enhanced NLO effects. Finally, we discuss the prospect of van der-Waal’s (vdW’s) based 2D semiconductors as saturable absorbers (SA) that can, in turn be employed to improve the currently available NLO characterization techniques. Finally, we end with a Machine learning recipe to perform High throughput calculations to scan the 2D vdW’s materials and its heterostructures as SAs.
articles.summary_en: This review evaluates how reduced-dimensional semiconductors can enhance second- and third-order nonlinear optical responses and surveys methods for measuring them. It highlights 2D van der Waals materials and heterostructures as saturable absorbers, including machine-learning approaches for high-throughput screening.

articles.title_original: Photocatalytic Integrated CO 2 Capture and Conversion to Methanol Using Modified MXene Quantum Dots
articles.title_en: Modified MXene Quantum Dots Proposed for Photocatalytic CO₂ Capture and Methanol Conversion
articles.excerpt_original: With atmospheric CO₂ concentrations exceeding 420 ppm worldwide, the global climate crisis has intensified, establishing direct air capture and utilization (DACU) as a critical pathway toward achieving the "dual carbon" goals. However, the elevated energy demand and CO 2 inertness of conventional carbon capture technologies severely limit their practical applications. In response to these limitations,, MXene quantum dots (MQDs) have emerged as promising candidates for photocatalytic DAC-CO 2 reduction, owing to their quantum confinement effects, tunable bandgaps, and rich surface chemistry. Therefore, this study establishes a framework of "theory-design-mechanism" and proposes MQD-based photocatalytic systems through N/S co-doping, g-C 3 N 4 heterojunctions, and Cu single-atom engineering. Through literature synthesis and theoretical analysis, this study examines the effects of band structure engineering on charge separation, the influence of surface Lewis basic sites in CO 2 activation, and the potential catalytic mechanism of Cu sites for CO intermediate hydrogenation. The analysis shows that this design is theoretically conducive to addressing the challenges of adsorption/activation and directed multi-electron reduction conversion of CO 2 at ultra-low concentrations, and provides reference insights for the design of solar-driven negative-carbon conversion materials.
articles.summary_en: The study reviews and theoretically analyzes MXene quantum-dot systems incorporating N/S co-doping, g-C₃N₄ heterojunctions, and copper single atoms for direct-air CO₂ capture and photocatalytic reduction to methanol. Its conclusions are design-oriented and theoretical, identifying potential mechanisms for CO₂ activation and multi-electron conversion at low concentrations rather than reporting demonstrated performance.

articles.title_original: Edge-Dominated Twist Mechanics at van der Waals Interfaces
articles.title_en: Edge-Dominated Twist Mechanics Revealed at van der Waals Interfaces
articles.excerpt_original: Despite the pivotal role of twist in modulating physical properties at van der Waals (vdW) interfaces, the mechanics governing torsional response remain poorly understood. Here, we probe twist mechanics at homo- and heterogeneous vdW interfaces, together with their sliding behaviors within a unified experimental framework. For both systems, the peak torque scales nearly linearly with contact area, in contrast to predictions from linear elastic and rigid models. Remarkably, while the sliding friction of the two interfaces diverges by over three orders of magnitude owing to different scaling laws, the corresponding torque follows the same linear scaling and differs by only about twenty-fold. Large-scale atomistic simulations reveal an edge-dominated yielding mechanism for torsional motion, wherein elastic reconstruction shifts the effective load-bearing region toward the edges, eliminating torque from the contact interior. This mechanism contrasts with the bulk-mediated stress transmission governing translational sliding, a distinction rooted in the different loading geometries inherent to the two motion modes, where torsional loading necessitates perimeter actuation, whereas sliding enables center-driven loading. This symmetry-imposed divergence demonstrates that translational and torsional properties cannot be predicted from one another at vdW interfaces, providing critical insights for the design of dynamically reconfigurable micro- and nanoelectromechanical devices.
articles.summary_en: Experiments and atomistic simulations show that torsional response at van der Waals interfaces is governed by edge-dominated yielding, with torque scaling differently from sliding friction. The findings improve understanding of reconfigurable micro- and nanoelectromechanical devices.

articles.title_original: Influence of Defect and Doping on Graphene for sensing of Nitrogen Oxide: First Principle Analysis
articles.title_en: Study identifies platinum-doped graphene as a promising NO gas-sensing material
articles.excerpt_original: This paper analyzes graphene as a gas sensor to detect toxic nitrogen oxide (NO) gas by modifying the graphene surface with different doping and defects. Generally, dopants and defects are considered as material imperfection which degrade their performance. However, at the nanoscale level, they enhance material functionality for device applications. In this work, pristine, single vacancy defected, and transition metals (copper, gold, platinum) doped graphene sheets are explored as NO sensing materials. The sensing mechanism is assessed based on the electronic nature, charge transfer, adsorption energy, electrical properties (I-V), and sensitivity. The result shows that defected graphene has the highest adsorption energy of -8.316 eV and 56% sensitivity. However, this extremely strong chemisorption renders the sensor practically irreversible at room temperature, limiting its reusability. In contrast, platinum doped graphene has the highest sensitivity of 143% with lower adsorption energy of -3.201 eV, suggesting better suitability for practical gas sensor. Thus, the work presents a framework for the development of high-performance graphene-based gas sensor using targeted material engineering, specifically through doping and defect engineering.
articles.summary_en: First-principles analysis compares pristine, vacancy-defected, and copper-, gold-, and platinum-doped graphene for nitrogen oxide detection. articles.title_original: Bidirectionally excited dual PIT device based on graphene patterns on a flexible substrate
articles.title_en: Graphene-patterned flexible device enables tunable terahertz sensing and optical switching
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract In this work, a facile double-layer graphene-flexible substrate metamaterial device is developed, enabling the realization of dual plasmon-induced transparency (PIT) response. The device comprises rectangular and circular graphene patterned elements, in which the circular graphene is encapsulated between two polyimide (PI) layers, while the rectangular graphene is anchored on a PI substrate with air as the upper cladding. The electromagnetic characteristics of graphene can be dynamically modulated via varying the Fermi level, thus achieving active tunability of the PIT resonant frequency and transmission window performance. Plasmon-induced transparency devices are multifunctional, serving as both sensors and optical switches. The modulation effects and underlying mechanism of geometric parameters, Fermi level and incident polarization on the transmission spectrum of the device are systematically explored. This device is capable of serving as a refractive index sensor, with a maximum sensitivity of 1.3 THz/RIU. It can also be utilized as an optical switch. At the frequency of 5.18 THz under Y-polarized incident light, tuning the Fermi level enables the device to attain a maximum modulation depth of 89% and an extinction ratio up to 9.59 dB. In contrast, by regulating the incident polarization direction, the device achieves a peak modulation depth of 77.5% and a maximum extinction ratio of 6.48 dB. This designed device exhibits outstanding performance, showing promising application prospects in terahertz refractive index sensing and polarization-regulated optical switches.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a dual-layer graphene–polyimide metamaterial device with bidirectional plasmon-induced transparency. Simulations indicate tunable terahertz refractive-index sensing, reaching 1.3 THz/RIU sensitivity, and polarization- or electrically controlled optical switching with modulation depth up to 89%.

articles.title_original: Low‐Cost Polyethylene/Calcium Carbonate/Boron Nitride Composites With Highly Thermal Conductivity
articles.title_en: Low-Cost PE/CaCO₃/BN Composites Deliver 3.53 W/m·K Thermal Conductivity
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT The ongoing miniaturization, multifunctionalization, and integration of modern electronic devices lead to more and more heat generated. Therefore, developing thermal interface materials (TIMs) with high thermal conductivity (TC) is of great significance in effective thermal management. Polymers are selected for thermally conductive composites owing to their excellent properties, including stability and electrical insulation. However, achieving their high TC often requires adding a large amount of heat fillers to the polymer matrix, which inevitably increases costs. Thus, it remains a key challenge to develop polymer composites that simultaneously possess high TC and low cost. It is an effective approach to solve this problem by adding low‐cost mineral fillers. In this study, inexpensive and widely used calcium carbonate fillers were incorporated to fabricate low‐cost polyethylene/calcium carbonate/boron nitride (PE/CaCO 3 /BN) TIMs. The PE/CaCO 3 /BN composite (40/30/30, volume ratio) has a TC of 3.53 W/(m·K) and a tensile strength of 12.11 ± 2.30 MPa. Furthermore, the PE/CaCO 3 /BN composite also has good thermal stability; its TC decreases to 3.17 ± 0.09 W/(m·K) after 50 hot‐cold cycles, which is a reduction of 10.11% compared with that of the as‐prepared counterpart. This study offers an effective strategy to fabricate high thermally conductive composites at a low cost.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed polyethylene/calcium carbonate/boron nitride thermal interface composites using inexpensive mineral fillers. The optimized formulation achieved 3.53 W/m·K thermal conductivity and retained 3.17 W/m·K after 50 hot–cold cycles, supporting lower-cost thermal management materials for electronics.

articles.title_original: A Biodegradable ZK61 Composite Reinforced with β-Tricalcium Phosphate and BN Nanoplatelets: Simultaneous Enhancement of Mechanical Properties and In Vitro Degradation Behaviors

articles.excerpt_original: Hexagonal boron nitride nanoplatelets (BNNPs) are promising nanofillers for Mg matrix composites owing to their excellent mechanical properties and low density. In this research, we report the fabrication of ZK61 magnesium composites reinforced with a hybrid of BNNPs and β-tricalcium phosphate (TCP) using spark plasma sintering (SPS). The designed composites exhibit a dense microstructure characterized by refined α-Mg grains with β-TCP particles preferentially distributed along the α-Mg particle boundaries. In addition, trace amounts of interfacial products, such as Mg3N2 and MgB2, are detected to act as chemical anchoring phases, promoting stronger interfacial bonding. Notably, the composite containing 5.0 wt % β-TCP and 0.3 wt % BNNPs demonstrates a remarkable combination of strength and ductility, exhibiting a compressive yield strength of ∼132 MPa, an ultimate compressive strength of ∼380 MPa, and an elongation of ∼28.9%. This favorable balance of high strength and substantial plastic deformability highlights the synergistic reinforcing effect of β-TCP and BNNPs in the ZK61 matrix. In addition, immersion tests reveal that the degradation rate of the 0.3BNNP/5TCP/ZK61 composite is approximately one-fourth that of the monolithic ZK61 alloy immersed in SBF for 28 d. These findings suggest that BNNP/β-TCP reinforced ZK61 composites are promising candidates for biodegradable implant materials.
articles.summary_en: Researchers fabricated ZK61 magnesium composites reinforced with boron nitride nanoplatelets and β-tricalcium phosphate using spark plasma sintering. articles.title_original: Spin–Strain Coupling and Direct Stark Response of the V B C B 0 Center in Monolayer hBN
articles.title_en: Calculations identify a strain-sensitive spin defect in monolayer hBN
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Spin defects in monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) can be positioned directly at an interface, making them attractive probes of local deformation. A useful strain probe, however, should respond strongly to strain without acquiring a comparable direct Stark shift. Here we use first-principles calculations to examine the neutral boron-vacancy–carbon complex V B C B 0 . For the planar geometry considered here, carbon substitution breaks the threefold symmetry of the parent V B − , concentrates the spin density on two undercoordinated nitrogen atoms, and rotates the principal zero-field-splitting axis into the hBN plane. At the PBE level the standard ZFS parameters are D = −4.537 GHz and |E| = 0.441 GHz (|E/D| = 0.097). The fixed-c tensor components exhibit large first-order biaxial-strain responses, dD c /dε = −341.8 and dE c /dε = +126.4 MHz/%, with distinct zigzag and armchair contributions and visible deviations from linearity over the ±2% range. In contrast, no linear clamped-ion response is resolved in the calculated spin–spin contribution to the ZFS tensor for an electric field applied along the in-plane principal axis; conservative full-ladder regression intervals bound |∂D c /∂F n | and |∂E c /∂F n | by 0.09 and 0.07 Hz·cm/V, respectively. These results identify V B C B 0 as a promising candidate for strain-sensitive spin spectroscopy and predict a pronounced strain dependence of its zero-field microwave transitions. Experimental identification of this center and demonstration of its optical spin readout remain the essential next tests.
articles.summary_en: First-principles calculations predict that the neutral boron-vacancy–carbon complex in monolayer hBN has strong biaxial-strain sensitivity and negligible linear Stark response. The defect could support strain-sensitive spin spectroscopy, but experimental identification and optical readout remain outstanding.

articles.title_original: Adsorption Properties of CO2 on both Pristine and B-doped Coronene Quantum Dots: A Density Functional Theory Study
articles.title_en: Boron-Doped Coronene Quantum Dots Show Potential for CO₂ Sensing
articles.excerpt_original: The study of the interactions between nanomaterials and target molecules at the molecular level is a key factor in the design of new materials for high-performance applications of nanosensors. In this study, the adsorption properties of CO2 molecules on the surface of pristine Coronene quantum dots (pCQDs) and Boron-doped Coronene (B-CQDs) clusters were estimated using density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The results show that CO2 molecules are weakly adsorbed (physisorption) on the pristine Coronene surface, while they are strongly chemisorbed on the B-Coronene surface with a large adsorption energy. The recovery time for CO2 on the pristine Coronene is very short, which makes the practical detection of this molecule almost impossible, regardless of any intrinsic electronic sensitivity. The substitution of a carbon atom in the Coronene framework with a Boron atom greatly enhances the adsorption properties. This change increases the chemical reactivity of the system favoring stronger interactions. The electrical conductivity of the B-Coronene cluster is greatly enhanced after the interaction with the CO2 molecule, and the energy gap exhibits a drastic change. Therefore, the B-Coronene cluster is a very promising nanosensor candidate for CO2 detection based on its high electrical sensitivity. Therefore, Boron dopants greatly promote the chemisorption of CO2 and enhance the overall sensing performance of Coronene. Overall, boron-doped coronene clusters demonstrate significant potential for application in the design and development of highly sensitive and efficient CO₂ gas detection systems.
articles.summary_en: Density functional theory indicates that boron doping strengthens CO₂ adsorption on coronene quantum dots, shifting interactions from weak physisorption to strong chemisorption. The resulting conductivity and band-gap changes suggest potential for sensitive CO₂ nanosensors, although the findings are theoretical.

articles.title_original: Non-Hermitian reconstruction of hybridized hyperbolic shear polaritons
articles.title_en: Dissipation enables reconfigurable shear polaritons in twisted van der Waals heterostructures
articles.excerpt_original: Hyperbolic shear polaritons (HShPs) represent a distinctive class of anisotropic polaritonic states that enable directional subwavelength light manipulation through asymmetric momentum-space dispersion, while their control in twisted systems has so far relied mainly on geometric and spectral parameters. Here, we introduce non-Hermitian dissipation as an additional degree of freedom for tuning HShPs in twisted van der Waals heterostructures. In twisted α-MoO3/α-V2O5 heterostructures with closely matched isofrequency contours but distinct dielectric losses, dissipation modifies the complex hybrid polaritonic states and thereby tunes the resulting momentum-space and real-space asymmetry. Near-field infrared imaging combined with analytical modeling and full-wave simulations reveals the evolution of the shear response with twist angle, excitation frequency, layer thickness, and substrate dielectric environment. The interplay between material dissipation and dielectric screening enables continuous regulation of the shear degree and reversible switching between shear-off and shear-on states. Furthermore, we demonstrate a proof-of-concept binary-state encoding scheme based on dissipation-controlled shear-state switching. Our work identifies non-Hermitian dissipation as an additional control parameter in twisted polaritonic systems, expanding the available design space for reconfigurable mid-infrared nanophotonics.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrate that non-Hermitian dissipation can continuously tune hybridized hyperbolic shear polaritons in twisted α-MoO3/α-V2O5 heterostructures. The approach enables reversible shear-state switching and proof-of-concept binary encoding for reconfigurable mid-infrared nanophotonics.

articles.title_original: Electron beam driven collective self hybridized exciton polaritons
articles.title_en: Electron beams strengthen collective exciton–polariton coupling in layered perovskites
articles.excerpt_original: Self-hybridized exciton polaritons in layered semiconductors emerge from the hybridization of excitonic resonances with confined photonic modes in films and provide a versatile platform for controlling light--matter interactions at the nanoscale. Yet, the nature of exciton--photon interactions and the collective and synchronous strong coupling of multiple excitons to the same photonic mode remain largely unexplored. Here, we use complementary momentum-resolved photoluminescence and cathodoluminescence spectroscopy to compare self-hybridized exciton polaritons in Ruddlesden--Popper perovskite flakes under optical and electron-beam excitation. We find that cathodoluminescence exhibits remarkably larger polaritonic level repulsion than photoluminescence, revealing an enhanced effective coupling strength under electron-beam excitation. We attribute this enhancement to the collective coherent excitation of multiple excitons by fast electrons, which couple to the same photonic mode and increase the interaction strength according to a $g_N=g_1\sqrt{N}$ scaling, with an effective number of up to $N\approx23$ coherently coupled excitonic oscillators. By reducing the electron kinetic energy, we further uncover a crossover to a partially incoherent excitation regime in which higher-order Fabry--Pérot exciton-polariton resonances disappear, leaving only the lowest polariton branches while coherent transition radiation persists. This transition arises because low-energy electrons excite excitons over extended spatial volumes, washing out the phase coherence required to sustain collective coupling and form polaritonic resonances. articles.summary_en: Researchers show that cathodoluminescence produces stronger exciton–photon coupling than optical excitation in Ruddlesden–Popper perovskite flakes, coherently engaging up to approximately 23 excitonic oscillators. The findings establish electron beams as a means to control collective light–matter interactions in layered semiconductors and clarify how reduced electron energy suppresses coherence.

articles.title_original: Self-Trapping Enabled Highly Bright Momentum-Indirect Interlayer Excitons
articles.title_en: Bright Exciton Emission Demonstrated in Perovskite–TMD Heterostructures
articles.excerpt_original: Interlayer excitons in two dimensional material heterostructures exhibit large exciton binding energies and long lifetimes, making them ideal platforms for studying excitonic devices and many body quantum phenomena. However, the spatially separated electron and hole nature of IXs reduces their oscillator strength by two orders of magnitude compared to intralayer excitons. Achieving high efficiency IX emission remains challenging and requires optimal material selection with appropriate momentum matching and meticulous device fabrication. Here we demonstrate a highly bright momentum indirect IX emission within heterostructures formed between 2D perovskites and monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides. The quantum yield of IX emission reaches 35.2% on average, over 50 times higher than that of the corresponding constituent TMD monolayer, with the highest value exceeding 60%. Notably, the radiative recombination efficiency of this momentum indirect IX exceeds that of momentum direct IXs in monolayer TMD-based heterostructures by two orders of magnitude. We suggest that the remarkably bright IX emission in our heterostructure originates from IX self trapping, induced by strong exciton phonon coupling arising from the soft lattice nature of the 2D perovskite. Our findings provide new insights into achieving high IX emission efficiency and open new avenues for exploring long lifetime excitonic devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated highly bright momentum-indirect interlayer exciton emission in heterostructures combining 2D perovskites with monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides. Exciton quantum yield reached 35.2% on average, with peak values above 60%, attributed to self-trapping driven by strong exciton–phonon coupling.

articles.title_original: Gut microbiota responses to two-dimensional materials: insights from in vivo models and in vitro antibacterial studies
articles.title_en: Review Examines How Graphene-Based Materials Affect Gut Microbiota
articles.excerpt_original: Two-dimensional (2D) materials are increasingly applied in environmental and biomedical fields, raising concerns about their interactions with the gut microbiota following oral exposure. In this review, we summarize current understanding of the effects of 2D materials, ranging from graphene-based materials (GBMs) to emerging 2D materials such as transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) and transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes), on the gut microbiota and the associated biological outcomes. We first summarize in vivo studies, mainly using mouse and zebrafish models and focusing on GBMs, demonstrating that 2D materials exposure can induce gut microbiota dysbiosis, often in association with local and systemic host responses. To provide mechanistic insights, we further examine how key physicochemical properties, particularly nanosheet dimensions, surface chemistry, and material transformation, determine the interactions between 2D materials and bacterial cells, drawing from the extensive body of in vitro antibacterial research. Finally, we highlight future research directions beyond the need for more efforts on emerging 2D materials, including linking physicochemical properties of 2D materials to microbial responses in vivo and analyzing the temporal response patterns of the gut microbiota. We also emphasize the development of community-relevant in vitro models and the need to dissect the potential biotransformation of 2D materials by the gut microbiota. A deeper understanding of the interactions between 2D materials and the gut microbiota will not only advance the safety assessment of these materials but also foster the development of safer-by-design 2D materials.
articles.summary_en: A review of in vivo and in vitro evidence finds that graphene-based and other two-dimensional materials can disrupt gut microbiota and trigger host responses. It identifies nanosheet dimensions, surface chemistry, transformation, and biotransformation as priorities for safety assessment and safer-by-design development.

articles.title_original: Achieving Ohmic and High‐Tunneling‐Probability Contacts in 2D Semiconductors via Hydrogen‐Bond‐Mediated Interfacial Coupling
articles.title_en: Hydrogen-Bonded MXene Contacts Improve 2D Semiconductor Injection
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Developing high‐performance electronics with two‐dimensional (2D) semiconductors is often hindered by high contact resistance at metal/semiconductor interfaces, which arises from the Schottky barrier for carrier injection and tunneling barrier for carrier transport. Conventional contact engineering faces a fundamental compromise: strong interfacial coupling induces Fermi‐level pinning (FLP), while weak van der Waals interactions mitigate FLP but introduces a large tunneling barrier. Here, we overcome this compromise by employing MXene electrodes on Janus MGeSiN 4 (M = Mo, W) semiconductors and modulating the interfacial interaction strength. Through selective surface termination of MXenes, Schottky, n‐type Ohmic, or p‐type Ohmic contacts can be achieved. Notably, medium‐strength interfacial coupling driven by hydrogen bonding in OH‐terminated MXene (OH‐MXene)/MGeSiN 4 contacts enables simultaneous Ohmic behavior and high tunneling probability. Specifically, the tunneling probability of OH‐MXene contacts ranges from 37.91% to 61.92%, with the maximum for Ti 3 C 2 (OH) 2 /WGeSiN 4 on the Si‐N side, significantly higher than F/O‐terminated MXene contacts (1.87% – 6.19%). Quantum transport simulations confirm superior current transport and charge injection efficiency in OH‐MXene/MGeSiN 4 devices. Furthermore, the Sure Independence Screening and Sparsifying Operator method identifies key descriptors governing both Schottky and tunneling barriers. Our results provide an efficient strategy for designing high‐performance contacts in 2D electronic devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers propose OH-terminated MXene electrodes with hydrogen-bond-mediated coupling to achieve Ohmic contacts and higher tunneling probabilities in Janus MGeSiN4 semiconductors. Simulations indicate substantially improved charge injection compared with fluorine- or oxygen-terminated MXenes, offering a design strategy for 2D electronics.

articles.title_original: Sensing Performances of Hierarchical Nano-Layered V2O5 Structures and Ab Intio Calculation of Their Gas-Adsorption Properties
articles.title_en: V2O5 Nanostructures for Gas Sensing
articles.excerpt_original: Significant research efforts have recently focused on nanomaterial processing for gas sensors and related sensing applications. However, the major challenges in the field involve the choice of material for the sensing layer of the sensor device element, together with the right structure, assembly, and morphology through which the full sensing properties of the material can be realised. Herein, we critically review the hierarchical nanostructures of V2O5 nanomaterial for application in gas sensing technology. Beyond the sheet structure, which serves as the fundamental building block of the V2O5’smolecular arrangement, nanostructures ranging from nanobelts to nanowires, nanorods, nanoribbons, nanofibres, nanotubes, and thin films were discovered as preferred configurations and thermodynamically favourable structures, according to many synthesis processes. Ethanol (C2H5OH) and Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) gases were identified as preferred molecules commonly detected by various V2O5 morphologies, with the nanotube structure showing preferential sensitivity and selectivity to C2H5OH. We also discuss perspectives from density functional theory (DFT) studies of V2O5 nanostructures and other (2D) materials structures for gas sensing applications. The studies highlight enhanced adsorption energy, increase conductivity, and band gap variation as a result of an upper shift in the Fermi level, all as a consequence of surface interaction between semiconductor crystal orientation and chemical molecules. Finally, our calculations of the optimised parameters for α-V2O5 orthorhombic structure showed good agreement with experimental and other theoretical data in the literature. The adsorption energy profile for NO2 molecules revealed that the Ag-doped surface exhibits the most negative adsorp
articles.summary_en: The study reviews hierarchical vanadium pentoxide nanostructures, including nanotubes, nanowires and thin films, for detecting ethanol and nitrogen dioxide. It combines experimental literature with first-principles analysis, finding that morphology and surface interactions influence adsorption, conductivity and selectivity, with silver-doped surfaces showing particularly strong NO2 adsorption.

articles.title_original: Programming Ion Transport in Phenyl‐Bridged Graphene Layers via Delocalization‐Catalyzed Decoupling
articles.title_en: Phenyl-Bridged Graphene Layers Improve Ion Transport for Desalination
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Graphene nanomaterials have shown extraordinary potential in capacitive deionization, but their actual performance often falls far short of theoretical predictions due to limited ion diffusion caused by narrow interlayer spacing. More importantly, the relationship between interlayer spacing and desalination efficiency remains unclear, hindering rational design. Here, we develop a delocalization‐catalyzed decoupling strategy that simultaneously regulates the interlayer structure and local electronic environment of phenyl‐bridged holey reduced graphene oxide. In this concept, phenyl bridging induces interlayer expansion and weakens direct graphene–graphene coupling, whereas the associated phenyl–graphene conjugation gives rise to interfacial charge redistribution and electron delocalization that facilitate charge and ion transport within the decoupled layered architecture. Crucially, we establish a semi‐quantitative correlation framework connecting interlayer structure, local electronic environment, local ion distribution, and macroscopic electrochemical behavior. This mechanistic insight advances our understanding of the structure‐activity relationship in layered materials. The electrode exhibited an ultra‐high desalination capacity of 80.6 mg g − 1 , an excellent adsorption rate of 16.12 mg g − 1 min − 1 , and outstanding stability with a capacity retention rate of 93.6% after 450 cycles, which exceeds previously reported. This study provides a semi‐quantitative correlation framework and methodological guidance for the rational design of 2D materials in ion capture and transport.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed phenyl-bridged holey reduced graphene oxide electrodes that expand interlayer spacing and enhance ion and charge transport. The electrode achieved a desalination capacity of 80.6 mg g−1, an adsorption rate of 16.12 mg g−1 min−1, and 93.6% capacity retention after 450 cycles.

articles.title_original: Deterministic Switching‐Path Engineering of CMOS‐Integrated 2D Memristors for Neuromorphic Computing
articles.title_en: CMOS-Integrated MoTe₂ Memristors Enable Controlled Neuromorphic Switching
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional (2D) memristors are promising for low‐power and high‐speed neuromorphic hardware. However, their performance under circuit‐level constraints remains limited because resistive switching relies on native defects, hindering precise control of filament formation. Here, we report 2D MoTe 2 memristors that integrate deterministic switching‐path density engineering with CMOS‐compatible one‐transistor‐one‐memristor (1T‐1 M) architectures. The devices exhibit highly linear and symmetric synaptic plasticity (α p /α d = 0.019/0.2), enabled by a balanced interplay between filament formation and confinement. Furthermore, monolithic integration with silicon transistors enables gate‐tunable compliance control, which suppresses variability and stabilizes array‐level operation. The resulting 1T‐1 M arrays exhibit a wide dynamic range (∼22×), and minimal potentiation/depression variation (7.95%/6.22%). Device‐aware simulations based on multilayer perception, convolutional neural network, and autoencoder models confirm improved learning accuracy compared to passive arrays. This work establishes a materials‐to‐circuit design framework that links defect‐path engineering with transistor‐assisted current control, providing a practical pathway toward 2D neuromorphic hardware.
articles.summary_en: Researchers engineered deterministic switching paths in 2D MoTe₂ memristors integrated with silicon transistors. The resulting 1T–1M arrays showed improved linearity, stability, dynamic range, and simulated learning accuracy for neuromorphic hardware.

articles.title_original: Symmetry breaking induces room-temperature interface ferroelectricity in two-dimensional metastable mosaic-like heterostructures
articles.title_en: Symmetry Breaking Enables Room-Temperature Ferroelectricity in Metastable Oxide Heterostructures
articles.excerpt_original: Metastable structures exhibiting unique properties hold significant potential for electronic applications. However, their inherent tendency to transform into thermodynamically more stable phases presents substantial challenges, as the stabilization of such metastable phases typically necessitates extreme conditions and complex synthesis strategy. Here, we demonstrate the synthesis of a metastable SmO2/Sm2O3 mosaic-like lateral heterostructure using molten eutectic salt. While both SmO2 and Sm2O3 are individually centrosymmetric, interfacial symmetry breaking at the junction simultaneously suppresses screw symmetry and inversion symmetry, resulting in a locally non-centrosymmetric configuration with broken spatial inversion. This structural asymmetry induces an intrinsic built-in dipole, a nonlinear optical response, and room-temperature interface ferroelectric polarization. Furthermore, vertically oriented interfaces provide confined pathways for directional ion transport, suppressing non-directional diffusion. Memristors based on the metastable heterostructure exhibit high performance, characterized by a maximum on/off ratio exceeding 109, switching speeds as fast as 47.3 ns, and retention times surpassing 104 s. The switching mechanism is consistent with field-driven oxygen vacancy migration along the vertical heterointerface, regulated by reversible oxygen adsorption and desorption at the electrode. This work offers a potential route for developing high-performance memristors leveraging metastable oxide heterointerfaces with coupled ferroelectric-like polarization and resistive switching functionalities. articles.summary_en: Researchers synthesized a metastable SmO2/Sm2O3 lateral heterostructure whose symmetry-broken interfaces exhibit room-temperature ferroelectric polarization and directional ion transport. Memristors based on the structure achieved an on/off ratio above 10^9, switching speeds as fast as 47.3 ns, and retention exceeding 10^4 seconds.

articles.title_original: Enhanced raman spectroscopy substrate based on graphene oxide for rhodamine 6 G detection
articles.title_en: Graphene Oxide SERS Substrate Enhances Rhodamine 6G Detection
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is widely employed as a highly sensitive technique for detecting various target molecules. Here, we prepared a metal-free graphene oxide (GO) -based SERS substrate. GO was deposited on a SiO₂/Si substrate for Rhodamine 6 G (R6G) molecule detection. The GO SERS substrate shows a significant enhancement as compared to the bare SiO₂/Si substrate due to its superior analyte adsorption and chemical enhancement effects. It demonstrates relatively higher enhancement than the graphene substrate. The intensity of the 613 cm⁻¹ peak exhibited about five times enhancement relative to the graphene substrate. Superior enhancement is likely attributed to the electronegative oxygen functional groups present in GO, which can generate strong local electric fields which enhanced the Raman signal. In addition, these functional groups may also enhance the adsorption efficiency of R6G molecules. The simple and cost-effective non-metallic SERS substrate is suitable for detecting harmful dyes like R6G, contributing to improved food safety and environmental monitoring.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a metal-free graphene oxide substrate for surface-enhanced Raman scattering detection of Rhodamine 6G. Oxygen functional groups improved analyte adsorption and produced approximately fivefold greater signal enhancement than a graphene substrate, supporting potential food-safety and environmental-monitoring applications.

articles.title_original: Effect of ambient temperature on optical and electronic response of deposited graphene
articles.title_en: Ambient Temperature Alters Graphene’s Optical and Electronic Response
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Optoelectronic functionalities based on graphene are realized at room temperature and on substrates, but predictive modeling often treats idealized, static, cryogenic structures. In this work we deliver a finite-temperature, substrate-realistic description of graphene’s electronic and optical response by combining Born–Oppenheimer molecular dynamics with real-time TD-DFTB. Using a graphene flake deposited on quartz as a model platform, we compute the temperature-dependent density of states, Fermi-level statistics, and linear absorption from an ensemble of thermally accessible geometries. We show that ambient thermal motion produces nonnegligible modifications of the near-Fermi electronic structure and systematically alters spectral line shapes through feature broadening and intensity redistribution. A comparison with experimental spectra qualitatively supports the approach, highlighting the importance of finite-temperature sampling for modeling supported graphene under realistic operating conditions. By relying on a carefully constructed computational protocol, this approach successfully captures the correct surface chemistry and the dynamic optical and electronic details of 2D material interfaces, which remain inaccessible throughpurely classical molecular dynamics or static periodic boundary calculations. As a result, our computational protocol shows great potential for providing intuitive qualitative insights into the design of nano-electronic and sensing devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used finite-temperature molecular dynamics and real-time TD-DFTB calculations to model graphene deposited on quartz under realistic conditions. The results show thermal motion modifies near-Fermi electronic structure and broadens or redistributes optical spectral features, informing graphene-based nanoelectronics and sensors.

articles.title_original: Extreme-bandwidth valley photonic metamaterials approaching Dirac velocity
articles.title_en: Valley photonic metamaterials achieve extreme bandwidth and near-Dirac velocity
articles.excerpt_original: Valley photonics supports edge transport robust to sharp bends and disorder. However, conventional valley states, typically developed within a quantized valley Chern number framework, remain limited group velocity and bandwidth, restricting their applicability in high-speed, high-capacity on-chip transport. By relaxing the use of a sizable valley Chern number as the primary constraint in performance optimization, we leverage Dirac-mass engineering and electromagnetic mode control to simultaneously enhance the bandwidth and group velocity of valley transport. By combining extreme inversion-symmetry breaking with effective suppression of mode mixing, the platform restores an approximately scale-invariant interfacial mass profile, enabling both a maximized valley bandgap and a near-Dirac group velocity. Near-field measurements directly confirm unidirectional valley propagation with deep-subwavelength confinement and robustness against sharp bends. The system supports estimated error-free transmission at 2 Gbps and an open eye at symbol rates approaching the carrier frequency, with a carrier-normalized symbol rate exceeding those of previously reported valley photonic platforms by more than one order of magnitude. These findings establish a practical design route for high-performance valley photonics, offering ultrabroadband, high-velocity, and compact signal transport with potential applications in high-capacity photonic interconnect. The authors demonstrate ultrabroadband valley transport with near-Dirac group velocity through Dirac-mass engineering and mode control.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report valley photonic metamaterials combining near-Dirac group velocity, ultrawide bandwidth and robust, deep-subwavelength signal transport. The platform demonstrated estimated error-free transmission at 2 Gbps and could enable higher-capacity on-chip photonic interconnects.

articles.title_original: Atomistic Modeling of W/h-BN/Graphene Multilayer Coatings for the Protection of the First Wall of a Fusion Reactor: Concept Justification, Validation of Neural Network Potentials, and the First Stage of the Study
articles.title_en: Modeling graphene multilayer coatings for fusion-reactor walls
articles.excerpt_original: The paper considers the degradation of the first wall of a fusion reactor under the combined action of helium fluxes, hydrogen isotopes, and fast neutrons. The standard wall material, tungsten, is destroyed due to helium erosion, hydrogen embrittlement, and neutron cascades. A multilayer protective coating architecture is proposed: a tungsten substrate providing heat removal; a hexagonal boron nitride layer enriched with boron-10 intended for neutron absorption; and an outer graphene barrier limiting the penetration of helium and hydrogen isotopes. The modeling was performed by molecular dynamics with neural network potentials in the GPUMD package. The universal NEP89 potential covering the elements W, B, N, and C was chosen as the main potential. Validation was carried out: the tungsten lattice parameter was reproduced with a deviation of 0%, and the C-C bond lengths in graphene and B-N bonds in h-BN were reproduced with deviations of 0.02% and 0.06%, respectively. It was established that the three-layer system remains structurally stable at 1200 K, and the layers do not mix. The adhesion energy of the W/h-BN interface is -16.48 eV, which indicates stable interlayer bonding. A separate test showed that NEP89 is unsuitable for describing the interaction of He with tungsten: the predicted insertion energy was -41.7 eV, whereas the DFT value lies in the range of +4...+6 eV. This result justifies the need to train a specialized potential for helium, which determines the next task of the study. This work is the first stage of a single study, the results of which will be combined into a final article for a peer-reviewed journal.
articles.summary_en: Atomistic simulations assess a tungsten/h-BN/graphene multilayer coating designed to absorb neutrons, remove heat, and limit helium and hydrogen-isotope penetration. The structure remains stable at 1200 K, but the study identifies a need for a specialized helium-interaction potential before further validation.

articles.title_original: Extended Framework Semiconductors (EFSs): A Unique and Efficient Platform for Synergetic Piezo‐Photocatalysis
articles.title_en: Extended Framework Semiconductors for Piezo-Photocatalysis
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Piezo‐photocatalysis is a compelling solution to synergistically merge their respective advantages. However, research on piezo‐photocatalysis has focused on inorganic semiconductors recently. Some studies and reviews have demonstrated the potential of organic semiconductor‐based materials, but these efforts remain fragmented due to the absence of a unified classification. Here, we introduce a unifying concept, extended framework semiconductors (EFSs), to categorize a broad family of 2D or 3D periodic networks constructed via covalent, coordination, or hydrogen bonding interactions. This family includes crystalline carbon nitrides (polyheptazine imide (PHI) and polytriazine imide (PTI)), semicrystalline graphitic carbon nitride (g‐C 3 N 4 , C 3 N 5 ), covalent organic frameworks (COFs), metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), and hydrogen‐bonded organic frameworks (HOFs). EFSs uniquely combine tunable specific surface area, facile functionalization, controllable structural dynamics (flexibility in MOFs/COFs/HOFs and interlayer adaptability in layered carbon nitrides), and band structure tailorability, making them ideal platforms for piezo‐photocatalysis. This review systematically summarizes the research progress of EFSs‐based piezo‐photocatalysts, with an emphasis on their distinct advantages over conventional inorganics. We further outline design strategies including defect engineering, morphology regulation, noble‐metal modification, functional group introduction, and heterojunction construction, along with the underlying mechanisms for enhanced catalytic performance. Finally, we discuss current challenges and future prospects, charting a clear roadmap for the development of high‐efficiency EFSs‐based piezo‐photocatalysts.
articles.summary_en: A review proposes extended framework semiconductors (EFSs) as a unified platform spanning carbon nitrides, COFs, MOFs, and HOFs for piezo-photocatalysis. It highlights tunable surface area, functionalization, structural dynamics, and band structures, alongside strategies such as defect engineering and heterojunction construction to improve catalytic performance.

articles.title_original: Next-generation solar modules: thermoelectric-assisted photovoltaics with a photothermal layer for thermal management
articles.title_en: Photothermal 2D semiconductors improve thermoelectric photovoltaic module output
articles.excerpt_original: The utilization of solar integrated thermoelectric technology plays a crucial role in addressing the global energy crisis. Enhancing the performance of the integrated technology can be achieved by introducing a photothermal layer. This layer consists of a photothermal material that exhibits broad solar absorption, including the near-infrared (IR) region. Wide-bandgap 2D semiconductor materials were used as the photothermal material. The integration shows better performance than other conventional techniques. This work includes an evaluation using COMSOL, a computational technique. Simulation models were developed and used to predict performance under various solar irradiance conditions. Results were predicted for electrical parameters and found to be 6.2 V produced by an individual module, whereas when the photothermal layer is introduced between the integrated technology, the device can produce a voltage of approximately 9 V. These findings include the comparison study of different photothermal materials. Thus, the proposed work involves predicting and optimizing the behavior of the integrated device in various environmental conditions and provides a way to maximize its energy conversion efficiency.
articles.summary_en: A computational study evaluates integrating a broad-spectrum photothermal layer made from wide-bandgap 2D semiconductors into thermoelectric-assisted photovoltaic modules. COMSOL simulations predict voltage increasing from 6.2 V to approximately 9 V under the modeled conditions, although the findings are not independently validated experimentally.

bulletin.title: Graphene Weekly Bulletin — Week ending 2026-09-13
bulletin.introduction: Commercial momentum is emerging most visibly in graphene-enhanced polymers and thermal management, with initial orders, product launches and consumer-device integrations indicating broader application testing rather than mature demand. Production and financing activity also point to efforts to build scale and strategic channels, though disclosed economics and performance validation remain uneven. Research continues to widen the opportunity set across membranes, coatings, thermal films, construction materials and optoelectronics, while underscoring formulation and durability trade-offs that will shape commercialization.

academic.blurb: Sodium molten-salt treatment was used during graphitization to flatten wrinkles in graphene platelets. The resulting 10-µm graphitic films reached reported thermal conductivity of 1,994 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, a specific and potentially consequential result for high-performance thermal-management films.

Technical-grade graphene and graphene oxide at 1 wt% were evaluated in cement mortar using multiscale pore characterization. The additives reduced capillary water absorption by 22% and 15%, respectively, without appreciably changing compressive strength, while altering pore morphology and distribution.

Graphene nanoplatelet geometry, loading, and additives materially affected HDPE mechanics. Higher loadings raised stiffness and tensile strength but reduced impact resistance; a copolymer and slip agent substantially improved ductility without sacrificing modulus or strength, clarifying formulation trade-offs in polymer composites.

Reduced-graphene-oxide photodetectors were fabricated with visible-to-near-infrared response and reported peak responsivity of 0.5 A/W at 650 nm under 5 V bias. The work emphasizes low-power operation and potential CMOS integration for optical sensing, biomedical diagnostics, and environmental monitoring.
